item.text:
I've sent the report to the parent agent. There is no single "call a model" path. Four dispatch switches in `utils` each pick the provider, plus eino's own, and each has its own request builders and retry loops. Underneath, three JSON POST helpers and two SSE POST helpers are near-copies that differ in small ways. `utils/provider.go` is 25 lines and only fills in a missing provider.

Three findings look like real bugs rather than just duplication:
- **Marking timeout:** marking's Google streaming and the Google tool path send through the chat helper. That caps them at `CHAT_DIRECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (max 600s) even when `MARKING_DIRECT_TIMEOUT_MS` is raised (up to 30 minutes).
- **eino misroutes providers:** `eino_runtime` quietly sends Anthropic, Groq, Nvidia, NetMind and the Google AI Studio account to Google. It also makes a single attempt through `InvokeMarkingDirect` with its own failover loop, so it skips Vertex routing, the retry budget and backoff. Its only user is quiz streaming in `handlers/gpt_quiz_eino.go`.
- **Wrong Google account:** the moderation classifier and research Google calls never set the Google account, so the named "Google (info@…)" accounts fall back to the default backend there.

The rest of the report covers:
- **Model selection:** there is one database resolver, `ResolveModelPlan`, which runs when a prompt is loaded. Several hardcoded defaults and env overrides sit alongside it. Vertex weighted routing only applies inside the four `Invoke*WithFallback*` functions. The main marking loop in `mark.go`, eino, research and moderation don't use it.
- **Cross-cutting concerns:** no shared invoker writes prompt logs, runs moderation or sends errors to Sentry. Callers do that themselves, and only moderation reports to Sentry. There is no token or cost tracking and no OTel anywhere in `utils`. Azure config is resolved in three places, and chat and marking read the endpoint env vars in opposite order.
- **Duplication:** about 19 duplicated pieces, with file:line pairs. The clearest is two SSE parsers that are byte-identical (`sse.go:12` and `chat_direct.go:2598`).

`InvokeLambdaWithFallback` (`lambda.go:750`) has no callers. Several handlers also call providers directly, outside the shared layer: Gemini, Azure, transcribe, speech, genkit and the separate eino maths pipeline.

item.text:
I've sent the full report back to the calling agent. It confirms the fragmentation you suspected: about 6,300 lines of provider plumbing sit outside `utils/` and `handlers/`. Roughly 5,300 of those are independent HTTP clients that don't go through the shared code.

- **Five separate stacks with their own clients:** `course_creator.go`, `pdf_course_creator.go`, `scripts/practicepaper`, the Azure/Google adapters in `eino_maths_suggestion_questions`, and the one-off course tools under `tools/`.
- **The eino maths module's clients run in production.** It is a separate Go module, but the root module imports it and the API's worker process starts its job (`main.go:178`). Its roughly 2,200 lines of Azure, Google, image and vision clients duplicate what `eino_runtime/` already does on top of the shared code.
- **Seven Azure OpenAI clients** are built with different api-versions (from `2024-12-01-preview` to `2025-04-01-preview`), and there are two Responses API URL styles. The gpt-5.4 endpoint is looked up differently in four places, so the same model can hit different resources depending on the program.
- **Retry behaviour varies a lot.** `course_creator.go` has jittered backoff and honours Retry-After. The practice-paper client has no retry at all, and `eino_textbook` inherits that gap. The image code has its own queue and failover.
- **Two image-generation clients are near-copies,** and they check API keys in the opposite order. The practice-paper one reads a misspelt env var (`AZURE_OPENAI_FALLBACK_AUDTIO`) and has a specific Azure resource URL hardcoded as its default.
- **Programs that do reuse the shared code have to fake an HTTP request to call it,** in three different ways. One script sets its timeout by changing an environment variable.
- **`eino_textbook` has no clients of its own.** It wraps the practice-paper client and the textbook helper in `handlers/`. That means textbook generation runs on two runtimes: this one on eino and the one in `handlers/` on Genkit.

Nothing in `mcpserver/`, `services/`, `liveapi/` or `plugins/` calls a model directly. `server` and `quiz_analyzer` in the repo root are compiled binaries, not source.

The report has a per-program table (provider, transport, model selection, env vars, retry, timeout, JSON parsing) with file:line references, plus the full lists you asked for.
